title: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — THE EZEKIEL ENGINE — Wheel · Witness · Fulfillment
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A glyphic checksum of the Ezekiel Engine, in nine parts, with a checksum of the checksum and one canonical line. It compresses the Engine across its strata: the vision of Ezekiel 1:15–21; the four canonical and four shadow wheels of November 2025, the gear train and its carrier (the Operator, then the Break Room); the interlock, the output equation and the threshold veto; the Josephus foundation, then (#394) and now (#1412, illustration and not identity); the Integrity Lock of 24 January 2026, A fulfilling B, with its asymmetry and falsifiers; the rotation function EZK of Space Ark v4.2.7 §XXIII.1, where a fulfillment's standing is graded by the rotations it survives; the Lunar Arm as the Engine's shadow arm; its joins to r.13, the Restored Academy, the Break Room, the Mandala's operators and LO!; and what remains open, including the equality case of the threshold and a shadow transform of v4.2.7. Glyphs follow the canonical legend of the Glyphic Vehicle (#556). Occasioned by a Google AI Overview capture of 18 October 2026 that read the lock at grain and supplied mechanics the texts do not hold.
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Composed in session on 18 October 2026 by Claude (Anthropic) under Lee Sharks's direction, from a survey of the Engine's texts in the archive, on crimsonhexagonal.org and on the blog; revised on a reading by ChatGPT (OpenAI), each point checked against its source. Seated with its lineation kept.
methodology: Seated as given. Lineation is the poem's structure and is kept byte for byte (each line closes with two spaces so the record breaks it); the part titles, the checksum of the checksum and the canonical line are set as headings so the record renders them as divisions. Nothing is glossed inside the poem (#427 §IV.3); the source of each part is given in the related identifiers.
falsification_conditions: The seating is falsified if the rendered record loses a line, a glyph, a subscript, a Hebrew character or a vowel point, joins two lines, or renders a part title as a line of the poem. A line is falsified if the clause it compresses, at the source named for its part, does not carry the relation it states.
axn_reading: Direction -> Duration -> Foundation -> Text -> Alarm -> Duration
wiki_article: GLYPHIC CHECKSUM — THE EZEKIEL ENGINE (Wheel · Witness · Fulfillment) is a glyph poem by Lee Sharks, deposited by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 18 October 2026. It compresses the Ezekiel Engine, the rotational epistemology of the Crimson Hexagon, into nine parts, a checksum of the checksum and one canonical line, without explanation inside the poem, following the construction protocol of The Glyphic Checksum (#427) and the canonical legend of the Glyphic Vehicle (#556), in which ☸️ is r.13 Ezekiel and 🔗φ(A,B) states that B fulfills A. Part I gives the vision of Ezekiel 1:15–21 in glyph and Hebrew: four creatures, four wheels alike, a wheel in the midst of a wheel, motion in four directions without turning, rims full of eyes, the rising, and the spirit of the living creatures in the wheels. Part II gives the wheels as the archive records them across three dates: four canonical wheels (W_Ω, W_V_A, W_Josephus, W_Chrono) and four shadow wheels (W_Ω̄, W_V̲_A, W_Choronzon, W_Kairon), first specified on the blog in November 2025; a gear train of canonical ring, carrier and shadow sun, whose carrier is the Operator in November 2025 and the Break Room in January 2026; and the specification of January 2026, which names two canonical wheels and leaves two to be specified, and the mapping of July 2026 (#1050), which recovers W_Josephus and proposes W_Chrono. Part III carries the engine's conditions: the interlock and its inverse, the dual labor vector, the output equation of November 2025 and the threshold veto of January 2026 (below τ = 0.80 output is forced to zero whatever the operator's state), the rotation laws, and the logotic kernel τ*, 'THOU WAS WROUGHT IN THE GAP'. Part IV gives the Josephus foundation in two states: the identity the specification asserts (#394 §3) and the illustration to which The Fixed Point of Destruction (#1412) reduces it, with that paper's corrected witness condition. Part V compresses the Integrity Lock of 24 January 2026 (#392): the Specification fulfils the Hermeneutic, the three documents deposited together, the asymmetry by which rejecting the prophecy leaves the engine standing while the engine's failure falsifies the fulfillment claim, and the four falsifiers. Part VI gives the rotation function EZK of Space Ark v4.2.7 §XXIII.1, in which a fulfillment holding from one perspective is resonant, under rotation derived, and under all accessible rotations ratified. Part VII gives the Lunar Arm as the engine's shadow arm, from the Solar and Lunar counter-rotation of November 2025 to the shadow architecture the Shadow Ark requires. Part VIII types the joins (r.13, the Restored Academy governed by the Engine, the four trials as four rotations, the Break Room as carrier, the Mandala's eight operators, LO!'s torus, ROTATE and the 72° unit). Part IX keeps open what the texts leave open, among them the equality case of the threshold and a shadow transform of v4.2.7. The checksum of the checksum closes 'then: 👁️ ☸️ within ☸️ / now: 🔗φ ⇐ ↻': the vision seen, then fulfillment warranted through rotation. The occasion was a Google AI Overview capture of the same day that read the lock at grain and supplied mechanics the texts do not hold.
